triage.rulebook_article: FIA F1 Sporting Regulations Art. 33.3 - Causing an Avoidable Collision
triage.justification: Attacking driver HAMILTON failed to manage closing velocity (64.1 km/h) into the braking zone, causing an avoidable rear contact into defending driver LECLERC (AI) (minimum clearance 5.48m).

bulletin.event: Autódromo José Carlos Pace (Interlagos) Grand Prix
bulletin.headline: DECISION: CAR (HAMILTON) PENALTY
bulletin.infringement: FIA F1 Sporting Regulations Art. 33.3 - Causing an Avoidable Collision
bulletin.facts: At timestamp t=27.60s during the session, Car HAMILTON and Car LECLERC (AI) converged to a minimum center separation of 5.48m. Synchronized 20Hz telemetry recorded a longitudinal closing velocity of 64.1 km/h, an along-track gap of 5.46m, and a lateral clearance of 0.53m. Lateral convergence rate was 0.64 m/s with a chassis overlap ratio of 2.5%. Physical contact was established at t=27.60s.
bulletin.reasoning: The Stewards reviewed telemetry data, tracking radar projections, and GPS coordinate feeds. The evidence demonstrates that Car HAMILTON was wholly or predominantly to blame for the incident. Attacking driver HAMILTON failed to manage closing velocity (64.1 km/h) into the braking zone, causing an avoidable rear contact into defending driver LECLERC (AI) (minimum clearance 5.48m). The Stewards determine that this constitutes a breach of FIA F1 Sporting Regulations Art. 33.3 - Causing an Avoidable Collision. Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and Chapter 4 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.
